from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet Willa and her rotating laser beam line.",
            "She starts at an initial point on the plane.",
            "The beam rotates clockwise around this pivot point.",
            "When hitting another point, the pivot immediately switches.",
            "This creates the \"Windmill\" motion through the points."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout("Introduction to 'Willa the Windmill'", lecture_lines)
        
        # Points positions (A1-F6 grid)
        # Choosing spread out positions
        pos_p = self.grid['C2']
        pos_q = self.grid['D5']
        pos_others = [self.grid['A4'], self.grid['B6'], self.grid['F1']]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in 5 white points (#FFFFFF) at random positions. Label one 'P'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        dot_p = Dot(pos_p, color=WHITE)
        dot_q = Dot(pos_q, color=WHITE)
        dots_others = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=WHITE) for pos in pos_others])
        all_dots = VGroup(dot_p, dot_q, dots_others)
        
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(dot_p, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(all_dots), FadeIn(label_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # She starts at an initial point. Draw a yellow line (#FFFF00) passing through point 'P'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pivot tracking
        pivot_tracker = Dot(pos_p).set_opacity(0)
        self.add(pivot_tracker)
        
        # Angle tracker (initial angle: 60 degrees)
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(60 * DEGREES)
        
        # Laser beam line
        laser_line = Line(color="#FFFF00")
        
        def laser_updater(mob):
            p = pivot_tracker.get_center()
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            # Extend line far enough to cover the grid
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(p - 5 * direction, p + 5 * direction)
        
        laser_line.add_updater(laser_updater)
        
        self.play(Create(laser_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The beam rotates clockwise around this pivot point.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Calculate target angle to hit Q
        vec_pq = pos_q - pos_p
        # Clockwise rotation: angle decreases
        # Current angle is 60 deg. 
        # Target angle for Q (from P)
        target_angle = np.arctan2(vec_pq[1], vec_pq[0])
        
        # Ensure we rotate clockwise (angle decreases)
        if target_angle > angle_tracker.get_value():
            target_angle -= 2 * PI
            
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # When hitting another point, the pivot immediately switches.
        # Flash Q yellow.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        label_q = Text("Q", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(dot_q, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            dot_q.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.5),
            FadeIn(label_q)
        )
        self.play(dot_q.animate.scale(1/1.5))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Change 'P' to white and set the green color (#2ECC71) to 'Q' as the new pivot.
        # Continue rotation.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(
            dot_p.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            dot_q.animate.set_color("#2ECC71"),
            pivot_tracker.animate.move_to(pos_q)
        )
        
        # Continue rotating clockwise (further decrease angle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.increment_value(-60 * DEGREES), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite: Discrete vs. Continuous Motion"
        lines = [
            "The beam's rotation angle changes continuously over time.",
            "But the center of rotation jumps at discrete hits.",
            "No three points are collinear to keep pivots unique."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_PIVOT = "#2ECC71"  # Green
        COLOR_LINE = YELLOW
        COLOR_POINT = WHITE
        COLOR_X = "#E74C3C"      # Red

        # Points for the windmill part
        p1_pos = self.grid["B3"]
        p2_pos = self.grid["D4"]
        
        dot1 = Dot(p1_pos, color=COLOR_PIVOT, radius=0.1)
        dot2 = Dot(p2_pos, color=COLOR_POINT, radius=0.1)
        dots = VGroup(dot1, dot2)

        # Labels for clarity
        label1 = Text("P1", font_size=16).next_to(dot1, UP, buff=0.1)
        label2 = Text("P2", font_size=16).next_to(dot2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        labels = VGroup(label1, label2)

        # The line
        line = Line(start=LEFT*2.5, end=RIGHT*2.5, color=COLOR_LINE)
        line.move_to(p1_pos)
        
        # Angle tracker
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Line updater - rotates around a specific point
        # Using a mutable list to hold the pivot since functions in updaters close over variables
        pivot_data = [p1_pos]
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle_tracker.get_value()).move_to(pivot_data[0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.add(dots, labels, line)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Calculate target angle to hit P2
        target_vector = p2_pos - p1_pos
        target_angle = np.arctan2(target_vector[1], target_vector[0])
        
        # Rotate until hit (ensure we go in the positive direction if possible or just towards it)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(target_angle), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Flash and jump pivot
        flash = Circle(radius=0.3, color=COLOR_PIVOT, stroke_width=4).move_to(p2_pos)
        self.play(
            dot2.animate.set_color(COLOR_PIVOT),
            dot1.animate.set_color(COLOR_POINT),
            FadeIn(flash, scale=0.5),
            run_time=0.3
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(flash), run_time=0.2)
        
        # Update pivot point for the line updater
        pivot_data[0] = p2_pos
        
        # Continue rotating around P2
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.increment_value(PI/3), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Clear windmill elements
        self.play(FadeOut(dots, labels, line), run_time=0.5)

        # Demonstrate collinearity issue
        collinear_p1 = Dot(self.grid["C2"], color=COLOR_POINT)
        collinear_p2 = Dot(self.grid["C4"], color=COLOR_POINT)
        collinear_p3 = Dot(self.grid["C6"], color=COLOR_POINT)
        collinear_dots = VGroup(collinear_p1, collinear_p2, collinear_p3)
        
        dashed_line = DashedLine(
            start=self.grid["C1"], 
            end=self.grid["C6"], 
            color=WHITE, 
            dash_length=0.1
        )
        
        # Red X
        cross_line1 = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["D6"], color=COLOR_X, stroke_width=10)
        cross_line2 = Line(self.grid["D2"], self.grid["B6"], color=COLOR_X, stroke_width=10)
        red_x = VGroup(cross_line1, cross_line2)

        self.play(Create(collinear_dots))
        self.play(Create(dashed_line))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Create(red_x))
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup/transition state
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lines
        title_text = "The Magic Invariant: The Balancing Act"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The line divides the other points into two sets.",
            "Let's color points on each side differently to see.",
            "As the pivot switches, the side-counts remain perfectly balanced.",
            "This invariant property holds throughout the entire rotation.",
            "The number of points on each side never changes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_LINE = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_PIVOT = "#2ECC71"
        COLOR_LEFT = "#3498DB"
        COLOR_RIGHT = "#E74C3C"

        # Create points
        p_pivot = Dot(color=COLOR_PIVOT)
        p_l1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        p_l2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        p_r1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        p_r2 = Dot(color=WHITE)

        # Position points on grid
        self.place_at_grid(p_pivot, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(p_l1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(p_l2, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(p_r1, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(p_r2, 'E4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color match with the yellow line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_LINE)
        pivot_pos = p_pivot.get_center()
        # Initial vertical line (angle = PI/2)
        line = Line(pivot_pos + 3.5*UP, pivot_pos + 3.5*DOWN, color=COLOR_LINE, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.add(p_pivot, p_l1, p_l2, p_r1, p_r2)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color match with Blue points
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_LEFT)
        self.play(
            p_l1.animate.set_color(COLOR_LEFT),
            p_l2.animate.set_color(COLOR_LEFT),
            p_r1.animate.set_color(COLOR_RIGHT),
            p_r2.animate.set_color(COLOR_RIGHT),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Add labels for the counts (within 1 grid unit of objects)
        label_left = Text("Left: 2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LEFT)
        label_right = Text("Right: 2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(label_left, 'A2')
        self.place_at_grid(label_right, 'A4')
        self.play(Write(label_left), Write(label_right))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color match with the Green pivot
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_PIVOT)
        
        # Setup rotation using ValueTracker for the angle
        # Note: direction vector is [cos(angle), sin(angle), 0]
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(PI/2) 
        
        # Track the current pivot object to allow for pivot switches
        pivot_ref = [p_pivot]
        
        def update_line(m):
            ang = angle_tracker.get_value()
            center = pivot_ref[0].get_center()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang), 0])
            m.put_start_and_end_on(center - 4.0*direction, center + 4.0*direction)
            
        line.add_updater(update_line)
        
        # Target angle to hit p_r1 (at B4)
        # Vector D3(2.5, -0.8) -> B4(3.5, 1.2) is (1, 2)
        hit_angle = np.arctan2(2, 1)
        
        # Rotate clockwise (angle decreasing from PI/2 to hit_angle)
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(hit_angle), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Hit! Switch pivot as per instructions
        # "The old green pivot turns blue (#3498DB), and the hit red point turns green (#2ECC71)."
        old_p = pivot_ref[0]
        new_p = p_r1
        
        self.play(
            old_p.animate.set_color(COLOR_LEFT),
            new_p.animate.set_color(COLOR_PIVOT),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        # Update pivot reference for the updater
        pivot_ref[0] = new_p
        
        # Emphasize the invariant labels
        self.play(Indicate(label_left), Indicate(label_right))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        # Continue rotation to show stability
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(hit_angle - 0.5), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        # Final rotation and emphasis on the labels
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(hit_angle - 1.0), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(Circumscribe(VGroup(label_left, label_right)))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching storyboard data
        title_str = "The 180-Degree Flip"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Watch what happens after a full 180-degree rotation.",
            "The line's orientation has completely flipped its direction.",
            "Points once on the left are now on the right.",
            "For this swap, the line must hit every point.",
            "This proves the windmill visits every point eventually."
        ]
        
        # Format with bullets for layout
        bullet_lines = ["- " + line for line in lecture_lines]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, bullet_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_LINE = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_PIVOT = "#2ECC71"
        COLOR_RED = "#E74C3C"
        COLOR_BLUE = "#3498DB"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE))
        
        # Setup Grid Elements
        pivot_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_PIVOT)
        self.place_at_grid(pivot_dot, "C4")
        
        red_pts = VGroup(
            Dot(color=COLOR_RED),
            Dot(color=COLOR_RED)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(red_pts[0], "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(red_pts[1], "A3")
        
        blue_pts = VGroup(
            Dot(color=COLOR_BLUE),
            Dot(color=COLOR_BLUE)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(blue_pts[0], "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(blue_pts[1], "E5")
        
        all_dots = VGroup(pivot_dot, *red_pts, *blue_pts)
        self.add(all_dots)

        # Line and Orientation Arrow
        line = Line(DOWN * 2.5, UP * 2.5, color=COLOR_LINE)
        line.move_to(pivot_dot.get_center())
        
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=pivot_dot.get_center(),
            end=pivot_dot.get_center() + UP * 1.5,
            buff=0,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=6,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.25
        )
        
        windmill = VGroup(line, arrow)
        self.add(windmill)

        # Full 180-degree rotation clockwise
        self.play(Rotate(windmill, angle=-PI, about_point=pivot_dot.get_center()), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(Indicate(arrow, color=WHITE, scale_factor=1.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_BLUE))
        
        # Labels for line-relative sides
        label_line_left = Text("Line's Left", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        label_line_right = Text("Line's Right", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        
        # When arrow is DOWN, Line's Left is Screen-Right
        self.place_at_grid(label_line_left, "C6")
        self.place_at_grid(label_line_right, "C2")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(label_line_left), FadeIn(label_line_right))
        self.play(Indicate(blue_pts, color=COLOR_BLUE), Indicate(red_pts, color=COLOR_RED))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(label_line_left), FadeOut(label_line_right))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE))
        
        # Reset rotation for segment display
        self.play(Rotate(windmill, angle=PI, about_point=pivot_dot.get_center()), run_time=1)
        
        # Rotation in segments with flashes
        # Sequence: A3 (26.5), B3 (45), D5 (135), E5 (153)
        self.play(Rotate(windmill, angle=-26.5*DEGREES, about_point=pivot_dot.get_center()), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(Indicate(red_pts[1], color=COLOR_LINE))
        
        self.play(Rotate(windmill, angle=-(45-26.5)*DEGREES, about_point=pivot_dot.get_center()), run_time=0.5)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Since the state is finite, the process is periodic.",
            "The windmill returns to its start and repeats forever.",
            "This beautiful cycle connects every point in the set."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and the Eternal Cycle", lecture_lines)

        # Points setup
        # Use a spread of points in the right-side grid area
        points_coords = ["C2", "B4", "D5", "E3", "C5", "D1"]
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in points_coords])
        for dot, coord in zip(dots, points_coords):
            self.place_at_grid(dot, coord)
        
        self.add(dots)

        # Windmill line setup
        # Initial pivot is the first point (P)
        pivot_p = dots[0].get_center()
        # Line length 5.0 (2.5 on each side) to fit the right-side area comfortably
        line = Line(start=pivot_p + 2.5*LEFT, end=pivot_p + 2.5*RIGHT, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        # Start with an initial angle (e.g. 30 degrees)
        initial_angle = 30 * DEGREES
        line.rotate(initial_angle, about_point=pivot_p)
        self.add(line)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Since the state is finite, the process is periodic."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Fast-forward rotation, leaving thin gray (#808080) traces
        num_traces = 40
        traces = VGroup()
        for i in range(num_traces):
            # Vary angle and pivot to simulate the windmill movement
            # We cover a lot of rotation to show periodicity
            ang = initial_angle + i * (6 * PI / num_traces)
            p_idx = (i // 7) % len(dots)
            p = dots[p_idx].get_center()
            t = Line(p + 2.5*LEFT, p + 2.5*RIGHT, color="#808080", stroke_width=1).set_opacity(0.3)
            t.rotate(ang, about_point=p)
            traces.add(t)
        
        # Show traces appearing rapidly to represent "fast-forward"
        self.play(Create(traces, lag_ratio=0.03), run_time=2.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "The windmill returns to its start and repeats forever."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Return to starting point P and initial angle
        # Fade out the traces and emphasize the line returning to its start
        self.play(
            FadeOut(traces),
            line.animate.set_color(YELLOW).set_stroke(width=6),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Pulse the line to show it's "back" at start point P
        self.play(line.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(line.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.2)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "This beautiful cycle connects every point in the set."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        
        # Pulse all points in green (#2ECC71) to signify cycle completion
        pulse_color = "#2ECC71"
        self.play(
            *[dot.animate.set_color(pulse_color).scale(1.8) for dot in dots],
            run_time=0.6
        )
        self.play(
            *[dot.animate.scale(1/1.8) for dot in dots],
            run_time=0.4
        )
        self.play(
            *[dot.animate.scale(1.8) for dot in dots],
            run_time=0.6
        )
        self.play(
            *[dot.animate.scale(1/1.8) for dot in dots],
            run_time=0.4
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The IMO Windmill Problem: Geometry in Motion
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in competitive mathematics and geometry.

sections.title: Introduction to 'Willa the Windmill'
sections.content: Introduce the setup: A set of 'S' points on a plane. A character, 'Willa the Robot', holds a long straight laser beam (the line L). The line starts at a point P and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point Q, that point Q becomes the new pivot point (the center of rotation), and the line continues to rotate.
sections.example: Visual: A scattering of 5 dots (seeds) on a screen. Willa stands at one dot, her laser beam rotating like a clock hand. As it hits a second dot, the 'glow' transfers to that dot, and the beam keeps spinning.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Discrete vs. Continuous Motion
sections.content: Explain the concept of a 'Pivot Switch'. Ensure the audience understands that the line's angle changes continuously, but the center of rotation changes at discrete moments (collisions). Explain that no three points are collinear to keep the transitions clean.
sections.example: Graphic: A side-by-side comparison. A standard clock (fixed center) vs. the 'Windmill' (center jumping from a blue dot to a red dot as the line sweeps across).

sections.title: The Magic Invariant: The Balancing Act
sections.content: Introduce the 'k-points' concept. If there are 'n' points total, the line divides the rest of the points into two sets. Crucially, when the line rotates and hits a point, the number of points on either side of the line remains constant (except for the pivot point itself).
sections.example: Visual: Highlight 2 points in blue on the left of the line and 2 points in red on the right. As the line rotates 180 degrees and swaps pivots, show that there are always 2 points on each side, maintaining a '2-2 balance'.

sections.title: The 180-Degree Flip
sections.content: Demonstrate what happens when the line rotates exactly 180 degrees. Since the 'k-points' on the left must now be on the right (because the line has flipped its orientation), every point must have acted as a pivot at least once to allow the sets to 'permute'.
sections.example: Character Example: Willa starts with a 'North' pointing arrow on her head. After the beam rotates 180 degrees, her arrow points 'South'. To achieve this 'flip' while keeping the side-count constant, the line must have passed through every single point.

sections.title: Summary and the Eternal Cycle
sections.content: Conclude that the windmill process is periodic. Because there are a finite number of points and directions, the system will eventually return to its original state, proving that the 'Windmill' will visit every point infinitely often.
sections.example: Animation: Speed up the rotation. Watch as the laser traces a complex web connecting all dots, eventually returning to the starting point and starting the exact same pattern again.
